transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… work, mostly. I’m a maintenance worker, and I keep dropping the ball on stuff I’m supposed to remember—scheduled callbacks, work orders, little follow-ups I tell people I’ll handle and then I just… don’t. Not on purpose.

It’s gotten piled up enough that my supervisor basically said I needed to come in and get it looked at, because I’m trying to move up and I guess this is starting to make me look unreliable. Which is frustrating, because I know the job, I can do the work… it’s just all the keeping track of who I called, who I owe something to, what order was next—then somebody asks me about it later and I feel like I got caught flat-footed.
Do you find yourself forgetting things or having trouble keeping track of tasks in your personal life, like at home or with friends, or is this mostly just happening at work?

I mean… it’s mostly work that’s making it impossible to ignore. That’s what brought me in. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, even basic follow-ups I promised somebody I’d do, and then it piles up.

Like, I’ll tell myself, “I’ll get to that after this other job,” and then another request comes in, somebody stops me in the hallway, and by the time anyone asks, it’s like it fell out of my head. And now it’s gotten bad enough that work sent me here, basically, before I lose my chance at moving up.
Can you think of any situations outside of work—like at home, with family, or with friends—where you’ve had trouble remembering tasks or keeping track of things you agreed to do?

Yeah, I mean… I’m trying to think. It’s hard because the work stuff is what’s right in my face, you know? Like that’s what brought me here—scheduled callbacks, work orders, little follow-ups I told people I’d take care of, and then they just pile up.

At home it’s not as formal, so maybe I don’t notice it the same way. Like nobody’s handing me a work order at my kitchen table, you know? But the reason I’m here is definitely that I keep losing track of those promised tasks at work, and it got to the point where they basically said, “You need to get this looked at,” before I mess up my chance at moving up.
Outside of work, do you find yourself forgetting things you agreed to do, like chores, appointments, or plans with friends or family?

I mean, outside of work… maybe, but what’s really been blowing up is the work stuff. That’s the stuff I can point to. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and those little follow-ups where I tell somebody, “Yeah, I’ll take care of that,” and then by the end of the day it’s just buried under everything else.

And then, you know, people act like I don’t care, which drives me crazy, because I do. I’ve been doing maintenance a long time, I know how to fix things, I’m good with my hands—but the keeping track part, the who-needs-what and when I said I’d call back, that’s where it all piles up. It got to the point where work basically sent me here, because if I don’t get a handle on it, I might lose my shot at moving up.

When you're at home and there's no supervisor or formal system reminding you, do you still find it hard to start or finish tasks you know you should do—like laundry, fixing something that's broken, or even just calling a friend back?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, home doesn’t have, like, a ticket system, so it’s harder to explain, but it’s the same kind of thing.

Even at work, I’ll do the actual repair fine—like I’ll fix the thing, whatever it is—and then somehow the last step just doesn’t happen. Closing the ticket, labeling the panel, checking back with the tenant… those are the parts that slip. And then later somebody’s like, “Did you ever finish that?” and I’m thinking, well, yes and no, you know?

It’s not that I don’t know how to do the work. It’s that finishing all the little end pieces… I don’t know, they just don’t stay in front of me unless someone or some system keeps pushing it back at me.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble staying focused or keeping track of tasks even when you were in school as a kid?

Yeah… yeah, I was. I mean, I don’t know that anybody called it anything back then, but I remember that even in grade school I was like this.

Teachers would say I was bright, which was always the funny part—like, “She understands it, she can do the work”—but I’d lose the paper, or I’d only do part of the directions because I missed the rest, or I’d need somebody to remind me, “Hey, finish this before you move on.” And then I’d be digging through my desk, and you know those old desks with everything shoved inside? Mine was always a disaster.

I mean, I can remember specific teachers getting frustrated with me, not because I was trying to be difficult, but because I just… didn’t keep track of things the way other kids seemed to. So yeah, looking back, that was there way before the job stuff.
As a child, did you have trouble sitting still, staying quiet, or waiting your turn, or did people often tell you that you were overly active or impulsive?

I’m not really sure on that one. I don’t remember being the kid who was, like, bouncing off the walls or getting in trouble for running around.

I mean, my brothers were louder than me, so maybe compared to them I seemed quiet—my mom used to have this whole thing about “girls behave better,” which, I don’t know, families say stuff like that and then everybody remembers it differently. But sitting still or waiting my turn… I can’t really point to anything specific. The stuff I remember more is school papers and directions and that kind of mess, not so much being overly active.
